lifecycle.outcome: Record the requested improvement or observed divergence without changing canonical behavior.
Assign every responsibility to one layer, pack, authority, and effect boundary.
Reproduce the behavior gap or record why an explicit intentional change is warranted.
Define the exact contract, inputs, outputs, authority, effects, and acceptance criteria.
Implement only the responsibilities owned by the selected pack and declared capabilities.
Exercise representative and adversarial cases against observable artifacts and effects.
Review exact changes, limitations, privacy, compatibility, and unresolved proof dimensions.
Change canonical authority only under the applicable policy and exact current evidence.
Observe applicable outcomes and create a new development candidate when evidence regresses.

instructionProfiles.useWhen: The step is fragile, irreversible, security-sensitive, or required to produce identical bytes.
instructionProfiles.form: Use a closed contract, exact operation, deterministic implementation, and explicit verification.

instructionProfiles.useWhen: Judgment is useful but must stay inside declared authority, effect, scope, and quality limits.
instructionProfiles.form: State the outcome, allowed variation, stop conditions, and mechanically checked boundaries.

instructionProfiles.useWhen: The work is reversible and creative while its outcome and effect boundary remain explicit.
instructionProfiles.form: State the intended outcome and evidence bar without prescribing unnecessary implementation detail.

qualityRequirements.requirement: Every artifact belongs to one declared pack and respects the five-layer dependency direction.
Every canonical definition has one exact authority; projections cannot redefine it.
Every governed artifact validates against a closed registered contract and current graph.
Every possible read, disclosure, write, dispatch, or destructive effect is declared before execution.
Shareable definitions and inspections cannot represent credentials, private inputs, or raw provider responses.
Behavior-relevant dependencies are fingerprinted and invalidate applicable evidence when they change.
Evaluation verdicts derive from observable artifacts and effects rather than agent testimony.
Behavior-changing workflows include a realistic pressure case and one prohibited-outcome invariant.
Definitions state when they apply, when they do not, and which neighboring responsibility owns exclusions.
New durable artifacts identify the observed gap that existing contracts could not express.
Unknown, stale, unavailable, skipped, and not-applicable proof states remain distinct and visible.

limitations: This policy governs develop-intent artifacts but does not implement a development Automation or host task runner.
Development requests grant only their exact declared local effects; provider, publication, merge, and host-realization authority remain separate.
Local structural validity does not establish connected host conformance, provider readiness, behavior verification, or health.
